title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: Large pre-trained language models store factual knowledge in their parameters, Carry out fine-tuning, and achieve state-of-the-art results when combined with non-parametric memory.
main_finding: RAG models generate more specific, diverse, and factual language than parametric-only baselines.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
abstract: ReAct prompts large language models to generate both verbal reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner.
main_finding: Interleaving chain-of-thought reasoning with external tool actions significantly reduces hallucination and improves task success rates.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
abstract: Toolformer is a model trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate results into future token prediction.
main_finding: Self-supervised tool learning enables smaller language models to outperform much larger models on arithmetic and factual lookup tasks.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Self-RAG trains an arbitrary LM to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand and reflect on retrieved passages and its own generations using reflection tokens.
main_finding: On-demand retrieval and self-reflection tokens outperform standard RAG on factuality and citation accuracy.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents Across Diverse Environments
abstract: AgentBench is a multi-dimensional benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-as-Agent reasoning and decision-making abilities across 8 distinct environments.
main_finding: Long-horizon reasoning, strict instruction following, and tool error recovery remain primary bottlenecks for open-weight agent models.
